newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Metlife sees strong 97/98 earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Metlife sees strong 97/98 earnings growth.

text.p: South African insurer Metropolitan Life Ltd on Wednesday said it expected continued strong gains in earnings in the current financial year as well as growth in market share.

Announcing the group's results for the year to September 30, managing director Marius Smith said: "The outlook for recurring premium growth remains good and continued strong gains in earnings can be expected.
"We are confident of further increasing our market share in the next financial year."

In the past 12-month period Metlife earnings rose to 195 cents a share from 156 cents. A final dividend of 78.5 cents had been declared, bringing the total for the year to 130 cents from 103 cents before.
Metlife reported premium income exceeding two billion rand for the first time while total income rose 25 percent to 2.7 billion rand.
Smith said that according to First Bowring Consulting & Actuarial Services, Metlife had fallen back in the yield rankings of insurance companies.
"In the last two years we have not being doing as well in investor performance as before," he said.

He said the reason for this was that Metlife's investment strategy had been be more invested in fixed interest, which was unexpectedly volatile, than in the equities which had a strong run in the first four months of the firm's financial year.

Smith said he, however, remained convinced that the fixed interest market would probably outperform the equity market over the next financial year due to the rise in short-term interest rates and signs that the economy was slowing down.
